main_turf.bias_notes: Clockwise (right-handed). One of the tightest metropolitan tracks in Australia. A 1,578m oval featuring a very short 308m home straight and tight turns. The track creates a massive mathematical bias toward early front-runners ('E') and pocket pressers ('P') who can command the inside rail. Deep closers ('C') suffer severe traffic and distance penalties trying to sweep around the sharp turns.
main_turf.post_bias: EXTREME INSIDE BARRIER BIAS: Inside barriers (stalls 1–3) hold a massive advantage in 1100m, 1200m, and 1250m dashes to grab the rail before the sharp first bend. Draws 7+ face severe energy loss going wide around tight bends.

handicapping_angles.extreme_on_pace_and_rail_bias: Canterbury is notorious for its front-running bias. Aggressively upgrade horses with elite 1st-call gate speed ('E') drawn in Stalls 1–3. Severely downgrade deep back-markers unless a frantic multi-horse pace battle is projected.
handicapping_angles.sydney_night_racing_specialists: Canterbury hosts the famous Friday Night Racing series under lights. Stables like Chris Waller, Waterhouse & Bott, Bjorn Baker, James Cummings (Godolphin), and Michael, John & Wayne Hawkes dominate. Top Sydney jockeys (James McDonald, Tommy Berry, Nash Rawiller, Tim Clark) hold a massive tactical edge.
handicapping_angles.heavy_rain_wet_track_off_rail_lane: When Sydney rain hits Canterbury, the inside fence bogs down. Jockeys on wet nights fan 3–5 off the rail turning for home. Check early race patterns on Soft 7 / Heavy 8+ ground.
handicapping_angles.midweek_metro_to_saturday_class_bridge: Canterbury Wednesday midweek and Friday night races serve as the primary launching pad for future Saturday Metro and Stakes winners. Pay close attention to high-value Sydney maidens and BM72 handicaps.
